item.title: Dynamical quantum simulations as laboratories for quantum information
item.description: arXiv:2610.37589v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dynamical quantum simulations are commonly designed to access a particular response function or correlation function. Yet the underlying protocol prepares a family of many-body states that contains information well beyond the observable for which the simulation was originally designed. In this work, we explore the idea of using these states as laboratories for quantum information. As a case study, we consider the local-pulse protocols used to compute Green functions in finite XX and XXX spin chains, and we interpret opposite source rotations as encoding a classical bit into the many-body system. This allows us to follow how the resulting record propagates, how it is encoded across local subsystems, and how readily it can be accessed with different measurements. We also find a clear separation between representation and readout. While fermionic covariance data exactly reconstruct the signed response in the XX chain, simple spin measurements recover a larger fraction of the locally available information in the XXX chain. This reversed ordering persists when we move from finite-pulse discrimination to local source-angle estimation. Going beyond the source record, the same reduced states also allow us to reinterpret results in terms of Bell state recovery and quantum communication rates, as well as providing direct access to the evolving bipartite and genuine multipartite entanglement of the system. Our results show that dynamical quantum simulations developed for response calculations can naturally be used to ask a much broader set of quantum-information questions about the many-body states they already prepare.
item.dc:creator: Su Yeon Chang, Hailey S. Murray, Brian Barch, Greeshma Oruganti, Luis Pedro Garc\'ia-Pintos, Martin Larocca, Mark M. Wilde, M. Cerezo

item.title: Dissolution-induced mode transition of crack propagation in carbonate rocks: From brittle fracture to diffuse damage
item.description: arXiv:2604.10184v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In chemically reactive environments, the mechanical integrity of geomaterials is fundamentally compromised by solid matrix dissolution. In this study, we propose a fully coupled chemo-mechanical phase-field framework to capture the dynamic interplay between mineral dissolution and fracture propagation. A key feature of the proposed model is the dynamic coupling of local mass removal to the fracture length scale, while also incorporating the damage-accelerated reaction-diffusion processes. Our results capture the development of an enlarged fracture process zone driven by chemical mass removal. This chemically induced widening blunts the sharp crack tip, alleviating the near-tip stress concentrations and causing a pronounced degradation in material stiffness before failure. Furthermore, we reveal a distinct ductilization effect, characterized by a more gradual accumulation of damage and a delayed onset of macroscopic failure. We show that the transition between brittle and ductile failure modes is dictated by the competing timescales of chemical degradation and mechanical deformation. Highly acidic environments enhance matrix dissolution and promote ductile fracture, whereas rapid mechanical loading limits chemical interaction and preserves brittle failure mode.
item.dc:creator: Fanyu Wu, Chong Liu, Mingze Hu, Manolis Veveakis, Manman Hu

item.title: Sustainability-Aware Discovery of Dual-Atom Hydrogen Evolution Catalysts via a Unified Machine Learning Framework for Activity and Carbon Cost
item.description: arXiv:2605.29821v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Catalyst discovery for green hydrogen has optimized activity alone, deferring economic and environmental costs to stages where they disqualify otherwise promising candidates. Here we introduce a unified machine learning framework that screens catalytic activity and monetized carbon cost in a single pipeline. A machine learning potential predicts hydrogen evolution activity and stability at density-functional-theory accuracy. A second model, trained on published estimates of the social cost of carbon, converts each candidate's embodied CO2 into a monetary burden. Screening 460 graphene-supported dual-atom catalysts across 23 transition metals and 20 nitrogen-coordination motifs yields 26 active, synthesizable candidates. The two axes then conflict. The most active candidates span Mn-, Fe-, Zr-, Cr-, Cu-, Ni-, Ti-, Nb-, V-, Pd-, Au-, and Rh-based catalysts, indistinguishable in adsorption energy yet spanning a 58,000-fold range in carbon cost. Joint optimization selects Mn2@2Nf and Zr2@2Nc, matching the best precious-metal activity at tens-of-thousands-fold lower carbon cost, independent of catalyst loading.
item.dc:creator: Yanmei Zang, Hyun Gyu Park, Gi Beom Sim, Tae Hyeon Park, Ho Jin Lee, Xiaorong Zou, D. ChangMo Yang, Soohaeng Yoo Willow, Hye Jung Kim, Sunbin Yoo, Chang Woo Myung

item.title: Crystal forming ability of amorphous refractory metals under nanoindentation: a molecular dynamics study
item.description: arXiv:2607.26881v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Amorphous refractory metal coatings combine high hardness with chemical inertness, yet their metastability makes them prone to mechanically induced crystallisation (devitrification) under contact loading, and how readily such a glass re-orders to its parent body centred cubic (bcc) crystal is unknown across the refractory series. We prepared amorphous V, Nb, Mo, Ta and W by melt quenching to 300 K, benchmarked each interatomic potential against ab initio liquid radial distribution functions and self-diffusion coefficients, and probed them by large scale molecular dynamics nanoindentation. Indentation drives a localised amorphous to bcc transformation by bulk nucleation, growth and coalescence. A crystal forming ability (CFA), the maximum slope of the sigmoidal bcc fraction versus depth curve, spans about a factor of four and decreases as V > Mo > Nb > Ta > W; it falls with indenter velocity as CFA scales as v^(-m), with a mean exponent of 1.08, so CFA.v is nearly constant and the transformation rate is almost velocity independent. Transforming atoms carry excess non affine displacement and local shear strain, not hydrostatic pressure, marking a shear associated displacive pathway; the bulk driving force is largest for the most resistant element, W, so resistance tracks cohesive bond strength rather than the thermodynamic driving force. Early bcc like order correlates with the sharpness and depth of the transition, whereas the mechanical work to half transformation correlates with the peak density of persistent bcc clusters. A cluster population balance links nucleation, growth and coalescence to a terminal microstructure whose completeness does not follow the CFA order.
item.dc:creator: Prashant Dwivedi, Alberto Fraile, Tomas Polcar

item.title: EBSD and Subtle Crystallographic Differences - A Study of Resolving Interlayer Spacings in Nb-Ni and Nb-Co mu-phases
item.description: arXiv:2608.01210v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In ordered intermetallics, slight variations in lattice site occupancy and specific interlayer spacings have been identified as the sources of significant changes in critical resolved shear stress and therefore how a given phase may affect alloy properties. So far, atom positions and lattice site occupancies have traditionally been characterised by high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD), which are methods that offer either local detail or high statistical significance but not both. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), by contrast, provides high spatial resolution across large sample areas and therefore, has the potential to enable the local investigation of interlayer spacing and site lattice occupancy with improved statistical reliability. The objectives of the study are to benchmark EBSDs capability for resolving these subtle features and to correlate them with compositional and mechanical properties. In this case study, we therefore show that EBSD can resolve key crystallographic features of mu-phase intermetallics, specifically interlayer spacings. We combine pattern matching with large-scale dynamical simulations of template libraries guided by XRD based information on lattice parameters. For this, we generate structures that vary in the spacing between triple-layer and Kagome layer and in the site lattice occupancy of the 3a site. This approach successfully predicts the change of interlayer spacing between Kagome and triple layers in Nb-Co and Nb-Ni mu-phases, in good agreement with XRD and HR-TEM.

item.title: Decoding Oxygen K-edge Fingerprints of NCM-811 Degradation via Ab Initio Many-Body Theory and High-Throughput Screening of Crystal Proxies
item.description: arXiv:2609.02206v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The degradation of LiNi$_{0.8}$Co$_{0.1}$Mn$_{0.1}$O$_2$ (NCM-811) in Li-ion batteries produces complex transition-metal oxides and binary phases that fundamentally limit cathode performance. While identifying these degradation products via X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) is essential for mitigating electrochemical performance loss, interpretation remains challenging due to the structural complexity of real-world samples. In this work, we present an integrated theoretical-experimental framework combining high-resolution oxygen K-edge XAS with \textit{ab initio} simulations based on many-body perturbation theory and high-throughput screening from density functional theory. We first evaluate the spectroscopic fingerprints of eight layered, spinel, and nominal rock-salt reference oxides, identifying discrepancies between the idealized single-crystal bulk phase and experimental spectra. Using high-throughput screening to analyze the oxygen $p$-projected density of states of 38 distinct polymorphs of NiO, CoO, and MnO, we propose that the spectral differences can emerge, among other factors, from local structural variations represented here by simplified structural proxies. Our work establishes a viable and rigorous computational pathway to interpret the complex landscape of degraded battery materials.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Duarte-Ruiz, Timo Reents, Elmar Kataev, Raul Garcia-Diez, Regan G. Wilks, Marcus Baer, Caterina Cocchi

item.title: Symmetry-Based Parameter Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning for High-Throughput Calculation of Lattice Thermal Conductivity
item.description: arXiv:2610.29634v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate and efficient prediction of lattice thermal conductivity (LTC) is essential for developing materials for thermoelectric, microelectronic, and photovoltaic applications. Here, we present a methodology for high-throughput calculation of LTC across large datasets of compounds sharing a common crystal symmetry. Our approach combines fine-tuning of the MatterSim 1M universal machine-learned interatomic potential with LTC calculations based on the solution of the Boltzmann transport equation. We introduce a symmetry-based few-shot fine-tuning strategy (SBFS-FT) based on low-rank adaptation. In this approach, MatterSim 1M is fine-tuned on a small, carefully selected set of compounds that share a common crystal symmetry. The resulting potential is then applicable for accurate LTC calculations for compounds with this crystal symmetry, even if they were not included in the fine-tuning set. We tested our methodology on datasets of half-Heusler compounds (space group 216), materials with space group 225, and spinels (space group 227). We demonstrated that LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M fine-tuned using SBFS-FT exhibited a mean absolute relative difference from the reference results (obtained using moment tensor potentials and polyMLPs) 2-3 times smaller than that achieved with the non-fine-tuned MatterSim 1M potential. Moreover, the accuracy of LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M after SBFS-FT was comparable to that achieved using the MatterSim 1M potentials individually fine-tuned for each compound. Importantly, SBFS-FT enabled generation of the potential suitable for accurate LTC calculations across large compound datasets substantially faster than fine-tuning of MatterSim 1M for each compound individually, reducing the computational time by approximately a factor of 5-7 for a dataset of 100 compounds.

item.title: Protonic thermoelectric effect of Superionic H$_2$O and magnetic field generation in Uranus and Neptune
item.description: arXiv:2601.03659v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The origin of the anomalous magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune, with significant tilts and multi-dipole configurations, is central to understanding the internal structure and evolution of the ice giants. Recent investigations confirmed that superionic H$_2$O ice is thermodynamically stable and constitutes the dominant H$_2$O phase within their icy mantles. Here, we use deep learning and ab initio molecular dynamics to investigate the thermal and protonic transport properties of superionic H$_2$O ice. We demonstrate that superionic H$_2$O ice exhibits a pronounced protonic thermoelectric effect, with a maximum Seebeck coefficient that can reach $\sim 620$ $\mu$V K$^{-1}$ within the interior of Uranus, whereas Neptune's is lower, within the range of 570-585 $\mu$V K$^{-1}$. Consequently, the temperature gradients in the icy mantles can induce proton migration, thereby driving magnetic field generation. Based on this mechanism, and within a dipolar approximation that captures the mean field, the disparities in mean dipolar magnetic field strength between Uranus and Neptune can be explained exclusively by their differing internal temperature gradients, and the predicted mean field strengths are comparable to those observed by Voyager 2.
item.dc:creator: Daohong Liu, Wei Zhang, Yu He, Xinzhuan Guo, Chuanyu Zhang, Yang Sun

item.title: Quasi-flat and exact flat bands in patterned two-dimensional electron gases and honeycomb wire networks
item.description: arXiv:2602.06118v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the formation of flat bands in a two-dimensional electron gas patterned by a periodic triangular array of repulsive antidots. In the high-barrier, narrow-trench regime, the spectrum develops kagome-like band triplets, each comprising a nearly flat band and two dispersive bands, with wave functions concentrated along the potential-free trenches. The two lowest energy bands have a different character with graphene-like dispersion and wave functions localized near the junction centers. The appearance of the trench-concentrated nearly flat bands further motivates a honeycomb quantum graph model as an effective description of the narrow-trench limit. In the single-channel graph, destructive interference produces exact flat bands with compact localized eigenstates protected by the $D_3$ symmetry. Their energies obey a quantization condition determined by propagation along the links and scattering at the junctions. We then extend the analysis to a multichannel quantum graph and derive the most general junction scattering matrix compatible with $D_3$ symmetry. Even- and odd-parity transverse channels contain equivalent symmetry sectors, and $D_3$ symmetry therefore allows them to mix. This mode conversion can disrupt the destructive interference responsible for flat bands and generically gives those bands a finite width. Exact flatness is nevertheless retained when only one transverse-parity sector is active, or when an additional symmetry forbids mixing between the two sectors. These results connect the continuum antidot model to its quantum-graph limit and identify transverse-mode mixing as a mechanism that limits flatness in multichannel networks.
item.dc:creator: Chunxiao Liu, Igor Pishniak, Beno\^it Dou\c{c}ot, J\'er\^ome Cayssol

item.title: Electronic correlations and dynamical screening with ab initio quantum embedding
item.description: arXiv:2603.12336v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: First-principles descriptions of correlated quantum materials require a simultaneous treatment of strong local many-body effects and nonlocal dynamical screening. We present an efficient fully self-consistent implementation of $GW$+EDMFT that combines nonlocal correlations at the $GW$ level with a non-perturbative treatment of local correlations within extended dynamical mean-field theory (EDMFT), with a well-defined double-counting correction and a self-consistently determined impurity interaction. Self-consistency in both the Green's function and the dynamically screened interaction is essential for describing screening processes across energy scales. A key ingredient that makes it computationally feasible is the compression of two-particle correlation functions using interpolative separable density fitting (ISDF). Applying the scheme to the Mott insulator SrMnO$_3$ and the correlated metal LaNiO$_3$, we show that the self-consistent effective local interaction resolves the overscreening inherent to constrained-RPA approaches. For SrMnO$_3$, this stabilizes a Mott-insulating state in quantitative agreement with experiment, while for LaNiO$_3$ local EDMFT corrections yield a quasiparticle mass enhancement consistent with ARPES. These results establish fully self-consistent $GW$+EDMFT as a reliable \emph{ab initio} framework for strongly correlated quantum materials.

item.title: Electrically tunable Crossed Andreev Reflection in Bipolar Magnetic Semiconductors
item.description: arXiv:2605.15939v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) is a nonlocal quantum transport phenomenon that arises at the interfaces between a superconductor and two spatially separated metals. In this process, an electron incident from one metal combines with another electron originating from the other metal to form a Cooper pair in the SC. In this work, we theoretically investigate the quantum transport properties of a device comprising a central $s$-wave superconductor sandwiched between two bipolar magnetic semiconductor (BMS) leads. BMS materials possess a unique bandstructure where the conduction and valence bands are fully spin-polarized in opposite directions. By applying independent gate voltages to the two BMS leads, we selectively tune their chemical potentials to configure an antiparallel spin alignment at the Fermi energy. In the absence of spin-orbit coupling (SOC), this specific configuration perfectly suppresses both local Andreev reflection and direct electron tunneling (ET), thereby isolating and profoundly enhancing CAR. The introduction of Rashba SOC, however, induces spin-flip scattering that relaxes these strict selection constraints, yielding finite probabilities for competing scattering channels and subsequently reducing the overall CAR efficiency. Nevertheless, for SOC strengths below a critical threshold, CAR remains the dominant transport mechanism over ET. This proposed architecture provides a scalable, stray-field-free method to achieve purely electrostatic control over nonlocal transport, advancing the development of highly efficient superconducting spintronic devices.
item.dc:creator: Polireddi Naveen, Abhiram Soori

item.title: Revisiting spin Hamiltonian parameters in a Kitaev material via Bayesian optimization of magnetization curves
item.description: arXiv:2605.24857v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Determining the spin Hamiltonian of a magnetic compound is crucial for understanding its magnetic properties. A standard approach is to derive model parameters from ab initio calculations based on the crystal structure. However, the resulting Hamiltonian can depend sensitively on methodological details of the ab initio procedure. This issue is particularly evident in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$, a candidate Kitaev material. Here, we present an alternative, data-driven approach to determine the spin Hamiltonian parameters of $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ by Bayesian optimization of experimental magnetization curves along the $b$- and $c$-axis directions. We optimize five parameters, namely the Kitaev interaction $K$, off-diagonal interactions $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$, the Heisenberg interaction $J$, and the $c$-axis $g$-factor $g_c$. The parameter set that minimizes the cost function is $(K,\Gamma,\Gamma',J,g_c)=(-6.0, 7.5, -0.3, -1.75, 2.3)$, where the exchange couplings are in meV. We find that the cost function is insensitive to the absolute value of the Kitaev coupling $K$. Thus, the magnetization data alone do not determine its energy scale. The cost function also depends only weakly on $\Gamma'$ and $J$, while the optimization favors a large positive $\Gamma$. By computing the static spin structure factor, magnetic susceptibility, and specific heat, we show that these quantities favor the large-$\Gamma$ scenario over the small-$g_c$ scenario and that the parameter set that minimizes the cost function yields good agreement with the experimental structure factor and susceptibility, and qualitative agreement with the specific heat. The combination of Bayesian optimization and accurate low-energy solvers provides an effective approach for determining parameters of spin Hamiltonians. This methodology opens a systematic route to determining spin Hamiltonians in quantum magnets from experimental data.
item.dc:creator: Takahiro Misawa, Ryo Tamura, Kazuyoshi Yoshimi, Youhei Yamaji

item.title: Dichotomous electronic system in a bilayer Ni$^{1+}$ nickelate
item.description: arXiv:2606.10564v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: "Infinite layer" nickelates ${\cal R}$NiO$_2$ (${\cal R}$=rare earth), having empty apical O sites, become superconducting upon hole doping, stimulating research into the related sequence Nd$_{n+1}$Ni$^{+p}_n$O$_{2n+2}$, formal charge state $p$=1+$\frac{1}{n}$, $n$=2,3,4,...., with the $n$=5 member being found to be superconducting. The two layer system La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_{7-\delta}$, with $\delta$=0,$\frac{1}{2}$,1 ($p$=2.5,2,1.5) approaches the peak in the nickelate superconducting dome but shows no superconductivity. Newly reported La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_5$F reaches the Ni$^{1+}$ goal while, as we show, introducing a partially occupied electron band $E^*$, based on an interstitial density that extends over the three open "apical" layers and leads to a single cylindrical electron Fermi surface giving self-doping. The commonly inert Ni $d_{xz},d_{yz}$ orbitals partner with interstitial $E^*$ to provide an incipient non-analytic Dirac point, with the critical point being reachable by pressure or further F insertion. The $E^*$ electron cylinder and the conventional Ni $dp\sigma$ hole carriers combine to provide a two-fluid dichotomy of hole and electron quasiparticles, affecting normal state properties that should verify the dichotomous aspect of transport.
item.dc:creator: Young-Joon Song, K. -W. Lee, W. E. Pickett

item.title: Dispersive mode coupling in $p$-doped semiconductor nanomechanical resonators
item.description: arXiv:2606.17392v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Dispersive coupling between vibrational modes with different frequencies is a major nonlinear dynamical effect. We show that in $p$-doped semiconductors such coupling is strongly enhanced. Moreover, the coupling parameters increase with the order of the nonlinearity. The doping-induced dispersive coupling becomes much stronger than the intrinsic one already for moderately strong doping. Its dependence on the hole density is nonmonotonic, and the temperature dependence becomes nonmonotonic for higher densities. Relevant mesoscopic frequency fluctuations are briefly discussed. The results are applied to Si resonators, where doping is used to compensate the temperature dependence of a clock mode, whereas another low-frequency mode is used as a thermometer to enable temperature stabilization.
item.dc:creator: Ankang Liu, Mahmoud T. Elewa, Mark I. Dykman

item.title: Quantum fluctuation-driven transport crossover between two liquid states in distinguishable helium-4
item.description: arXiv:2607.23127v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show the emergence of a quantum fluctuation-driven transport crossover between two liquid states in distinguishable helium-4 obeying Boltzmann statistics, in the absence of atomic exchange. Using path integral centroid molecular dynamics simulations over 0.1-3.3 K and 1-60 bar, we investigate the transport properties of two distinct liquid states: the low quantum dispersion liquid (LQDL) and the high quantum dispersion liquid (HQDL). While LQDL exhibits conventional liquid behavior consistent with the Stokes-Einstein (SE) relation, HQDL emerges at lower temperatures and displays anomalous gas-like transport characterized by superdiffusion and ultralow viscosity, accompanied by a breakdown of the SE relation. This counterintuitive emergence of gas-like dynamics upon cooling reflects the dominant role of nuclear quantum fluctuations, in contrast to thermal fluctuations at higher temperatures. Across the LQDL-HQDL boundary, we identify a transport crossover marked by a qualitative change in the velocity autocorrelation function (VAF), a transition in the Prandtl number, and the emergence of transport minima in shear and kinematic viscosities, thermal conductivity, and thermal diffusivity. These minima reflect a crossover from liquid-like to gas-like transport upon cooling in the low-temperature subcritical region, in addition to the universal transport minima observed in the supercritical regime. The transition from oscillatory to monotonic VAF defines a second Frenkel line, distinct from the conventional Frenkel line observed in the supercritical region. LQDL is a heat-transport-dominated dissipative fluid, whereas HQDL is a momentum-dominated inertial fluid. These results demonstrate that nuclear quantum fluctuations alone induce gas-like liquid behavior and provide a unified picture of transport phenomena in distinguishable helium-4 without superfluidity.
